expects.rule: The first screen names the current game or the team's next match, with one action: wishlist, buy, play or watch.
Each game shows its platforms and links straight to the store page (Steam, console stores, app stores), not just platform logos.
A trailer or gameplay footage is playable on the page or one click away, with sound off by default.
A press kit page gives a fact sheet (release date, platforms, price, studio), logos and screenshots to download.
An esports team lists its rosters per game, upcoming matches with date and time, and results, kept current.
Studio, contact and careers links are reachable from every page; community links (Discord, Twitch) are labelled.

traits: 2 of 8 link to stores or show platforms per game (Milestone with PS5, Xbox, Steam, Epic and Switch icons; Glowing Cheetah with a Steam icon); none of the 8 has a wishlist button.
1 of 8 links a trailer per game (Milestone, to YouTube); the others show stills, illustrations or a playable page.
2 of 8 have a press kit link (Orma, Teka Teki); 1 has a careers page linked in the menu (Milestone).
Both esports teams (IGZIST, Flash Wolves) list divisions by game, players, sponsors and a merchandise section; only Flash Wolves shows a match score with date and time.
3 of 8 lead with a slogan rather than a game name (Ink 'Join the new era of gaming', Orma 'Lasciamo un'orma.', Glowing Cheetah 'We craft stories').
2 of 8 are not in English first (Orma in Italian, Flash Wolves in Traditional Chinese); Milestone offers an English and Italian switch.

sites.name: Milestone
sites.why: Italian racing-game developer: headline 'Hot Wheels Infinite Rush Out Now' with Watch the trailer, then a carousel of games each with release date and platform icons (PS5, Xbox Series, Steam, Epic, Switch). Menu Games, About us, News, Contact, Careers, EN/IT switch; news dated items for DLC and patches.

sites.name: Orma Games
sites.why: Small studio in Rome, page in Italian: headline 'Lasciamo un'orma.', top bar Giochi, Studio, Contatti, a catalogue of 3 titles (ECO tagged OUT NOW, two projects marked in development), side menu with Press kit and Newsletter, a contact form with an INVIA button. No store or wishlist button.

sites.name: INK Games
sites.why: Austin publisher: headline 'Join the new era of gaming', menu Games, Studio, Support with Login and Sign up, featured title Prize Kingdoms, a 'Play. Win. Earn.' three-step section, an octopus character illustration, a news block linking to 2024 and 2025 announcements. Cookie notice on load.

sites.name: Glowing Cheetah Studios
sites.why: Father-and-son indie studio: headline 'We craft stories', menu Projects, Team, Contact, two project cards (the game Pigeon's Mission, a novel marked Coming soon) with View project links, a 'Footage from Pigeon's Mission' strip of level sketches, a founders' story, Steam, Discord, Twitch and YouTube icons, a plain email address.

sites.name: Teka Teki Studios
sites.why: Indie studio page built as a desk of paper props: posters, sticky notes, a dog note and a developer photo on a table texture, no visible menu. A press kit page presents its game Two & Two: Agents, a two-player online co-op puzzle game, with capsule art only.

sites.name: IGZIST
sites.why: Japanese esports team: menu TEAM, MEMBER, STORE, EVENT, NEWS, VIDEOS, CONTACT with Twitter, YouTube and Twitch icons; divisions for VALORANT, Pokemon UNITE, Rainbow Six Siege, Apex Legends; player list, dated roster news (2026), merchandise with yen prices (T-shirt 4,900 yen), sponsor logos. No match calendar.

sites.name: Flash Wolves
sites.why: Taiwanese esports team founded 2012, page in Traditional Chinese with English labels: menu TEAM, EVENTS, NEWS, MEDIA, SPONSOR, PRODUCT; a lead news story on a Hearthstone player's retirement, teams for Arena of Valor, Teamfight Tactics, Street Fighter 6, KartRider, one match result FW vs DCG 4:2 with date and time, sponsor logos including Red Bull.

sites.name: Twitch Rivals
sites.why: Twitch's creator competition series: headline 'Beyond the win.', menu About, 3 New Series, FAQs, Brand Assets (zip download), Watch Now and View Schedule buttons, three series described (alt_arcade, hard_mode, casual_quest), partner logos. No event names, dates or prize amounts on the home page.

avoid: Platform logos with no link to the store page, so a player who wants the game has to search for it.
A home page for a tournament series with no event names, dates or prize amounts.
A press kit that holds one capsule image and no fact sheet, release date or screenshots.
An esports team page with rosters and merchandise but no upcoming match calendar.
A loading screen or sound toggle that must be passed before the game or studio is named.
Template placeholder text ('Lorem ipsum') left in a section near the footer, as seen on a recognised studio site.
Contact or press email addresses whose displayed text and link target differ.
